In process-intensive domains, such as the law, this is insufficient: information may be substantively correct yet procedurally irrelevant because it applies to a different stage of the user's matter. This paper introduces A2JRAG, a process-aware retrieval framework that conditions retrieval on an expert-authored Procedural State Graph (PSG). A PSG encodes process stages, transitions, contextual dimensions, mandatory guardrails, and escalation triggers. The evolution of RAG can be viewed in four dimensions: one-dimensional naive RAG retrieves flat facts; twodimensional relational RAG adds pairwise relationships and metadata; three-dimensional GraphRAG traverses entity-centered knowledge graphs; and four-dimensional A2JRAG adds the user's position along a temporal-procedural path. We formalize the PSG representation, describe a state-conditioned retrieval architecture, and present a planned workshop demonstration for legal self-help in North Carolina eviction proceedings. The contribution is a framework and evaluation agenda for reducing a distinct failure mode in legal AI systems: retrieval of legally accurate but procedurally mistimed and misaligned information.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.7114139","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,7,29]],"date-time":"2026-07-29T13:20:15Z","timestamp":1785331215000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["A2JRAG: Process-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Public Legal Information Systems"],"prefix":"10.2139","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0002-5249-2230","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Thomas","family":"Martin","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Scheree","family":"Gilchrist","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"78","deposited":{"date-parts":[[2026,7,29]],"date-time":"2026-07-29T13:20:16Z","timestamp":1785331216000},"score":39.029182,"resource":{"primary":{"URL":"https:\/\/www.ssrn.com\/abstract=7114139"}},"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"references-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.7114139","published":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"subtype":"preprint"},{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,6,12]],"date-time":"2026-06-12T16:03:42Z","timestamp":1781280222096,"version":"3.54.1"},"posted":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,26]]},"reference-count":0,"publisher":"Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,26]],"date-time":"2025-02-26T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1740528000000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"https:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"<jats:p>Digital content has grown exponentially,  requiring efficient and context-aware information retrieval systems. Search methods which utilize key word based functions, such as BM25, rely on lexical matching but often  fail to capture semantic relationships. Using dense vector embeddings models, Small  Language Models (SLMs) can improve retrieval accuracy, however Retrieval-Augmented  Generation (RAG) incorporates the concept of contextual ranking through generative artificial  intelligence to further enhance search relevance.\u00a0<\/jats:p>\n                <jats:p>An experiment on a single  document corpus and a cryptography-related query evaluates BM25, SLM  embeddings, and SLM + RAG for document retrieval.    Based on experimental results, BM25 achieves a moderate relevance score of 0.500, retrieving documents based on exact matches but lacking contextual  understanding.\u00a0 As SLM embeddings identify semantically similar concepts, they  increase recall for queries with conceptual variations and a relevance score    0.7668. SLM + RAG  outperforms both      approaches'         relevance score    0.9202, retrieving the most relevant document with accuracy and\u00a0 contextually enriched responses. A hybrid retrieval model  that combines dense embeddings and generative ranking improves search quality  substantially.\u00a0<\/jats:p>\n                <jats:p>This exploratory study has multiple implications for information  retrieval and including the need for scalable multi-document retrieval, FAISS\/DPR  integration for efficient vector searches, and domain-specific fine-tuning of  SLMs. Using this approach, enterprises can achieve faster, more accurate, and contextually aware  document retrieval by combining SLMs and RAG methods. Hybrid approaches could be  explored in large-scale retrieval settings, with stable workflow integration     processes     across  diverse industries like legal research, healthcare, government, and finance.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.36227\/techrxiv.174060240.09460752\/v1","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,26]],"date-time":"2025-02-26T15:40:19Z","timestamp":1740584419000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":1,"title":["Enhancing Context-Aware Search with Retrieval-Augmented Generation"],"prefix":"10.36227","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-0452-4894","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Rahul","family":"Shetty","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Institute of Health Policy, Management and Evaluation, Dalla Lana School of Public Health, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada."}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"263","link":[{"URL":"https:\/\/www.techrxiv.org\/doi\/pdf\/10.36227\/techrxiv.174060240.09460752\/v1","content-type":"unspecified","content-version":"vor","intended-application":"similarity-checking"}],"deposited":{"date-parts":[[2026,6,12]],"date-time":"2026-06-12T15:11:43Z","timestamp":1781277103000},"score":37.118183,"resource":{"primary":{"URL":"https:\/\/www.techrxiv.org\/doi\/full\/10.36227\/techrxiv.174060240.09460752\/v1"}},"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,26]]},"references-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.36227\/techrxiv.174060240.09460752\/v1","published":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,26]]},"subtype":"preprint"}],"items-per-page":3,"query":{"start-index":0,"search-terms":null}}}
